title: The sequencing atlas's references
set_out: Read the library floor on the 137 healthy sequenced samples; build the held-error reference from the 153 healthy inputs; find why the megakaryocyte column does not name donor 3; keep the B and T commissioning samples aligning.
open_at_turnover: Met-A for the sorted cell reads Normal on healthy samples from outside the atlas; Met-A for the whole sample and the territories read high on them too, and are next. GitHub's machines are free; nothing ahead of the sequencing instruments needs them.

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: The megakaryocyte donors read against each other
entries.what: The three megakaryocyte donors compared pairwise, and each with a monocyte and a lung macrophage input, by a new pair comparison tested on a known answer first.
entries.outcome: The donors agree with each other more than with the cells donor 3 was named as. The comparison's depth-weighted score had a fault (it averaged a ratio at each site) and was corrected; read again with it, donor 3 reads nearest megakaryocytes (development, on a spent donor; the committed test stays not met).

entries.title: Each healthy cell's held error, region by region
entries.what: The 153 healthy sequenced inputs' molecules counted on Google spot machines, pooled by cell into 14,133 regions beside the sequencing atlas.
entries.outcome: Built and in the chain: 56 cells. It is the reference IAM-A needs to read plasma once the Deconvolver has found what is in it.

entries.title: Each library's own floor
entries.what: Each of the 137 healthy sequenced samples' error rate at 46,989 sites where every healthy cell agrees completely, read by the one command.
entries.outcome: Not met: the floor is low (median 0.00625) and does not follow depth, and Met-A does not follow it. Library noise is not why shallower libraries read higher.

entries.title: The study read with the full chain
entries.what: All 36 samples read again from their saved alignment pieces with every reading the chain holds, each flagged.
entries.outcome: All 36 read; nine development readings ran on each, five were recorded as not run with the chain's reason.

entries.title: Replays with the full chain
entries.what: Seven earlier replays and two new ones (cervical self-samples, plasma cfDNA on arrays) sent with the full chain.
entries.outcome: Landed so far: aging, glioma blood, endothelial, stroke, Crohn's and colitis sorted cells, prostate, cervical; reference only.

entries.title: Blood drawn before a cancer diagnosis (reference only)
entries.what: The Italian prospective cohort's 329 bloods, drawn years before 146 breast cancer diagnoses, read with the full chain.
entries.outcome: Every cell's Met-A reads higher in the later cancers, and holds within slides; reference only, and blood drawn farther from diagnosis reads higher than nearer, so it needs its own test before it means anything.

entries.title: The Deconvolver on the sequencing atlas
entries.what: A sequenced sample split into its cells against the IAM Sequencing Atlas's own levels (56 cells, 5,599 marker sites), through the one command.
entries.outcome: 8 of 9 planted mixes read their shares; the ninth gave 8 % to close relatives of its cells. The share a pure cell gives others from counting alone is 1 to 2 %.

entries.title: The healthy full-chain pass on sequencing
entries.what: The 137 healthy sequenced samples read by the one command with the full chain, twice: before and after the in-mix readings moved onto the sequencing atlas.
entries.outcome: The C-Score, IAM-A and coupling-A read Normal on healthy samples; Met-A for the sorted cell (1.07), for the whole sample (1.09) and the territories read high. Purity does not explain it.

entries.title: The in-mix readings on the sequencing atlas
entries.what: Met-A for the whole sample, the territories and the C-Score per cell mixed from the sequencing atlas's counted levels at IAM-Atlas v2.1's sites.
entries.outcome: 6 of 6 constructed healthy samples read 0.97 to 1.02.

entries.title: The sky on sequencing
entries.what: The residual sky read against the sample's own mix of the sequencing atlas, after a fault that left holes in its map was fixed.
entries.outcome: None of 6 constructed healthy samples shows structure beyond the null; contiguous regional shifts are not what it reads, by construction.

entries.title: IAM-A in the sample's mix
entries.what: IAM-A for plasma and other mixed samples: held errors over the number the sample's own shares predict, from each cell's healthy held-error rate.
entries.outcome: Run 2 met: healthy mixes 0.991 to 0.993, every rate raised a fifth 1.190. Run 1 asked donor half A for a cell it does not hold.

entries.title: Met-A site by site
entries.what: Every identity site's reads, levels and disorder for 20 healthy samples, written by the one command.
entries.outcome: The excess sits where the reference level is near 0. Treating the reference as counted explains about 2 % of it. The two donor halves agree far more closely than counting allows, and the published counts equal each sample's own molecules, so the sites were chosen where these donors agree.

entries.title: Met-A on samples the atlas does not hold
entries.what: 35 healthy sequenced samples never read before and not atlas inputs: 25 control prefrontal neurons and 10 sorted pancreas samples, through the one command.
entries.outcome: The 25 neurons read Met-A 1.0132: sorted-cell Met-A reads Normal outside the atlas. The pancreas libraries cover too few identity sites to read. Met-A for the whole sample and the territories read high on the neurons too.
